summary:
We developed Torsion, an interactive tool designed to identify locations on Earth with terrain similar to selected regions of the Moon and Mars. The project uses elevation and terrain data to compare features such as slope, elevation, surface relief and roughness, allowing users to explore and rank potential lunar and Martian analogue locations on Earth.

This addresses the challenge of preparing for future space exploration by providing researchers with accessible environments where they can study and test technologies, equipment and mission strategies before deploying them beyond Earth. Instead of relying solely on simulations or waiting for space missions, researchers can use suitable Earth locations as practical testing grounds for extreme extraterrestrial environments.

Torsion is important because exploring the Moon and Mars will require extensive preparation, testing and understanding of unfamiliar terrain. By connecting planetary terrain with real locations on Earth, our project can make this preparation more practical, accessible and efficient. It also demonstrates how data analysis and technology can be applied to real challenges in space exploration while encouraging further research and innovation.
details:
This project features an interactive analysis tool which finds locations on Earth with similar geology and topography to chosen locations on the Moon and Mars. The program does this by using the NASA planetary data alongside Earth elevation data, and applying terrain analytics to find suitable analog locations.

Once the user has selected a location on the interactive planetary map, the tool will source elevation data from NASA’s Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) and Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA). Extractable terrain data such as elevation change, gradient, roughness and relief is then downloaded onto the website. This will create a set of numeric data points which represents the area.

The tool will then search through elevation data from Mapzen’s API using terrain elevation tiles to find locations on Earth with similar terrain. This elevation data is represented in the form of red, green and blue comparison graphs, as well as rendered 3D Models available on the website. These will then be converted into elevation values which are fed into a weighted similarity algorithm. The algorithm which will compare the values from the planet to the Earth locations and give a ranked list of the best analog locations, with viewable toggles for each of them.

An interactive tool will show the user potential locations, similarity score and location information. Using the 3D functionality API from Google Earth, the user can select a location to automatically be taken there. This allows them to visualize what the terrain looks like in a three dimensional space.

Our app was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python to process the geospatial data, NASA planetary data, Mapzen Terrain APIs, Google Maps Platform, GitHub and Vercel. This processes elevation data from rasters, converts the locations into coordinates, extracts the terrain features, and calculates how similar they are.

The main benefit of this project is that it is now significantly easier to find planetary analogs. Typically finding suitable analogs can involve substantial reading and documentation or manual searches. With this tool, we are able to provide users with a simple way of finding a larger range of locations to investigate using quantitative data.

The application can also be used to help choose where to test rovers on Earth; researching planetary surfaces, planning geological field work, and choosing suitable locations for simulated missions. Moreover, it serves as an educational tool for students to investigate the similarities and differences between the planetary landscapes.

This project also features creative aspects by featuring 3D point-to-point globes for all the planets, as well as a fully editable weighting algorithm, all built on open-source data. As a result, the tool is able to automate sampling of Earth locations with custom similarity scores and interactive 3D geolocation.

The development phase of our application included different coordinate systems, high processing requirements when sampling large areas of the Earth, and finding meaningful terrain features to compare. While considering the limitations of our system, we were able to note that similar topographical features don't directly translate to the same gravity, air pressure, radiation and geological makeup, affecting the accuracy of a chosen analog.

Overall, we aim to create an easily accessible tool which can be scaled. Through this project, we have organized and interpreted complex elevation data into a mathematical algorithm. This significantly aids planetary research, provides better access to scientific analysis and further innovation.
